newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares fall 0.18 pct in shallow trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares fall 0.18 pct in shallow trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell 0.18 percent in quiet trading at the start of weekly business on Saturday, maintaining last week's shallow drift downwards.

The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.26 points to 147.35 points in light trade worth just 219,000 dinars ($310,000). Brokers said they saw little sign of the market breaking out of its torpor this week.
"It's a tired market today. Very tired," said one trader.
Shares rose in three companies, with a combined turnover of just 3,500 dinars ($4,950). Nineteen stocks declined and another 11 traded but closed unchanged.
Jordan Gulf Bank and Arab Banking Group between them accounted for half of Saturday's turnover, but both closed unchanged at 0.89 dinars and 246 dinars respectively.
Market analysts Pearl Consulting said in its review of last week's trade that lack of institutional buying was pushing prices down to "extremely low levels".
"Many institutional investors realise that the period of stability at the Amman Financial Market is a golden opportunity to build up their portfolios...at relatively cheap price levels," it said.

But brokers say political gloom from Palestinian-Israeli deadlock over troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron and continued trade sanctions on neighbouring Iraq are casting shadows over the exchange.

The AFM index has been stuck for the seven weeks within a point either side of 147.7 points. Daily turnover has halved during the same period to around 500,000 dinars from about one million dinars a day in September.
